diseases.description: Apple scab is a fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis that affects apple trees worldwide. It causes lesions on leaves, fruit, and twigs and can reduce fruit quality and yield.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown lesions on leaves
Lesions may be circular or irregular
Severe infection can cause premature leaf drop
visual_signs: Dark olive or brown velvety spots on upper leaf surfaces
Raised scab lesions on fruit skin
Cracked, corky appearance of infected tissue
prevention: Remove and destroy fallen leaves and infected fruit
Apply appropriate fungicide programs during the growing season
management: Fungicide sprays timed to primary infection periods
sources: Cornell University Plant Disease Diagnostic Clinic — Apple Scab
Penn State Extension — Apple Disease Management

diseases.description: Black rot is a fungal disease that affects apple trees, causing leaf lesions, fruit rot, and cankers on branches and trunks.
symptoms: Brown leaf spots with concentric rings (frog-eye appearance)
Fruit rot starting at the calyx end
prevention: Prune out dead or cankered wood
management: Fungicide applications during bloom and post-harvest

diseases.description: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease that requires both apple and juniper (cedar) hosts. It causes bright orange-yellow spots on apple leaves and can defoliate trees.
symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces
visual_signs: Vivid orange or yellow leaf spots
Coral-like galls on juniper branches (alternate host)
Orange, finger-like projections on apple leaf undersides
prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar alternate hosts when practical
Apply fungicides during the infection window
management: Fungicide programs timed to juniper telial stage
Avoid planting apples near junipers in new orchards

Powdery mildew is a fungal disease affecting cherry leaves and fruit, characterized by white powdery fungal growth.
symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and shoots
visual_signs: White to gray powdery fungal growth on leaf surfaces
management: Fungicide applications during the growing season

diseases.disease: Cercospora Leaf Spot / Gray Leaf Spot
diseases.description: Gray leaf spot is a significant fungal disease of maize caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis, producing elongated rectangular lesions on leaves.
symptoms: Elongated, rectangular lesions parallel to leaf veins
Lesions turn gray to tan as they mature
visual_signs: Rectangular gray-brown lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions may coalesce in severe cases
management: Fungicide applications when threshold conditions are met

diseases.description: Common rust of corn is caused by Puccinia sorghi and produces reddish-brown pustules on leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Pustules appear on both leaf surfaces
Severe infection can cause leaf yellowing and premature death
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak spore periods
management: Fungicide use in high-value or severe infection situations

diseases.description: Northern leaf blight is a fungal disease of maize producing large cigar-shaped lesions on leaves.
visual_signs: Elliptical lesions up to several inches long
management: Fungicide applications when disease pressure warrants

Black rot is a major fungal disease of grapes causing fruit rot, leaf lesions, and cane infections.
symptoms: Circular leaf lesions with dark borders
Fruit shriveling into hard black mummies
visual_signs: Tan leaf spots with purple-brown borders
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and infected canes
management: Fungicide program from bloom through fruit development
sources: Penn State Extension — Grape Disease Management

diseases.description: Esca is a complex grapevine trunk disease involving several fungal pathogens. It causes leaf stripes, tiger-stripe patterns, and vine decline.
symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves (interveinal chlorosis and necrosis)
visual_signs: Yellow and brown interveinal striping on leaves
Red-brown wood with white sectors in cross-section

diseases.description: Grape leaf blight, also known as Isariopsis leaf spot, causes necrotic lesions on grape leaves.
symptoms: Premature leaf drop in severe cases
visual_signs: Irregular brown spots with darker margins
sources: IFV (Institut Français de la Vigne et du Vin)

Huanglongbing (HLB), or citrus greening, is a devastating bacterial disease transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid. It causes yellowing, misshapen fruit, and eventual tree decline.
visual_signs: Blotchy yellow mottle on one side of the leaf
Unevenly colored fruit with a distinctive green lopsided appearance
prevention: Remove and replace infected trees in high-pressure areas
management: Nutritional support to slow decline (does not cure)
sources: University of Florida IFAS — Citrus Greening
California Department of Food and Agriculture

diseases.description: Bacterial spot of peach and nectarine is caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni, producing leaf lesions, fruit spots, and gummosis.
symptoms: Shot-hole appearance as tissue falls out
visual_signs: Angular leaf lesions often limited by veins

Bacterial spot of pepper causes leaf, stem, and fruit lesions, reducing plant vigor and fruit quality.
symptoms: Small dark leaf spots with yellow halos
management: Cultural practices to reduce leaf wetness

Early blight is a fungal disease of potato caused by Alternaria solani, producing dark, target-like lesions on older leaves.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern)
Lesions begin on older, lower leaves
management: Fungicide programs beginning at canopy closure

diseases.description: Late blight is a destructive oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora infestans that can rapidly destroy potato foliage and tubers.
symptoms: White fungal growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions

Powdery mildew on squash and cucurbits is caused by Podosphaera xanthii and produces white powdery growth on leaves.
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surfaces
visual_signs: White powdery coating that can be rubbed off
management: Fungicide applications (sulfur, horticultural oils, or registered products)

diseases.description: Leaf scorch of strawberry is caused by Diplocarpon earlianum, producing irregular purplish-red to brown leaf lesions.
symptoms: Leaf margins turning brown and dry
management: Fungicide applications in autumn and spring

Bacterial spot of tomato is caused by several Xanthomonas species and produces small, dark lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit.
visual_signs: Dark angular spots limited by veins

diseases.description: Early blight is a common fungal disease of tomato caused by Alternaria solani, producing target-like lesions on older leaves.
symptoms: Dark brown lesions with concentric rings
management: Fungicide applications starting at first symptoms

diseases.description: Late blight of tomato is a fast-spreading oomycete disease that can destroy foliage and fruit within days under cool, wet conditions.
visual_signs: Dark, expanding lesions often starting at leaf tips or margins

diseases.description: Tomato leaf mold is a fungal disease common in greenhouses, caused by Passalora fulva (formerly Cladosporium fulvum), producing yellow upper leaf surfaces and olive-green mold on undersides.
symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to brown mold on lower surfaces
visual_signs: Velvety olive-green fungal growth on leaf undersides
management: Fungicide applications (registered products for leaf mold)

diseases.description: Septoria leaf spot is a fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici, producing numerous small circular leaf lesions with dark margins and tan centers.
symptoms: Dark brown margins with tan or gray centers

diseases.description: Two-spotted spider mites are arachnid pests that feed on tomato leaf cells, causing stippling, bronzing, and webbing.
symptoms: Fine white or yellow stippling on leaves
Fine webbing on leaf undersides and stems

diseases.description: Target spot of tomato is caused by Corynespora cassiicola and produces brown leaf lesions with concentric rings, similar in appearance to early blight.
symptoms: Lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit
visual_signs: Target-like lesions with alternating light and dark bands

diseases.description: TYLCV is a geminivirus transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). It causes severe leaf curling, yellowing, and stunting of tomato plants.
symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of young leaves

diseases.description: Tomato mosaic virus is a highly stable plant virus transmitted by mechanical contact, seed, and contaminated tools. It causes mottled leaf patterns and fruit deformation.
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaf patterns
Irregularly shaped fruit with internal browning
prevention: Disinfect tools and hands between plants
